## Behaviour
The reference labels issues `author:LOGIN` from the opener GitHub records and later needs `author backfill`. In the ledger the author is a fact already: the `actor` of the item's first event. Expose it: `qew list --author LOGIN` (case-insensitive), `qew show` prints `author`, imports keep the actor of the imported first event, and sync adds the label `author:LOGIN` to the mirrored issue. The author is never taken from a typed argument (no `--author` on create). An actor that cannot be a label (space, comma, over 50 characters) is a typed failure before any write, naming the item; an item whose first event has no actor shows 'unknown' and gets no label (not a guess). Items that already carry a manual `author:` label on the forge are not retagged. No backfill command is needed.

## Scenarios
- `author_comes_from_the_first_event_actor_only`: create as alice then set as bob: author stays alice; prevents re-attribution.
- `list_filter_matches_case_insensitively`: `--author Alice` finds alice's items.
- `actor_that_cannot_be_a_label_fails_before_any_write`: 'bad login,x' reported against the item, no forge call; prevents a half-labelled sync.
- `imported_item_without_an_actor_has_unknown_author_and_no_label`: no guess is mirrored.

## Reference coverage
Tests (author backfill walk, 6): labels every issue without an author from its recorded opener, dry run reports the plan, nothing to backfill is quiet, a login that cannot be a label is indeterminate before any write, overlay scope never touches unmanaged issues (covered by per-target select), labels that did not persist are indeterminate (covered by `board-write-verification`-style read-back; dropped as command). Backfill itself is dropped.

## Qew today
Missing. Events already store `actor` (ledger.md); nothing reads it for filtering or labelling.
seen.title: Derive each item's author from its first recorded event and expose it
